annotation_method: Road regions and visual notes drawn by AI-assisted review of the keyframe; provisional, not independently validated ground truth.
scope: Pre-recorded drone clips from Pexels illustrate a synthetic logistics scenario. All are top-down except the container-terminal queue, which is an oblique view. None shows the fictional CA-47 incident. The crash, clear-road and rest-area clips were not filmed near the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach; the sources of the two heavy-traffic clips do not state where they were filmed.

clips.title: Truck crash across travel lanes
clips.note: A jackknifed tractor-trailer and spilled load lie across the marked carriageway, with a second truck stopped beside it. No traffic passes the wreck in this direction. The opposite carriageway, outside the marked region, keeps moving.

clips.title: Same crash, closer pass
clips.note: The wrecked cab, its trailer and a fuel or fluid spill cover the marked carriageway, which is otherwise empty. Traffic on the far carriageway, outside the marked region, is moving. The detector does not recognise the jackknifed wreck as a vehicle, so the CV sees an empty road and stays inconclusive; the dispatcher can see the wreck and override it. The camera turns during the clip; the road region follows it.

clips.title: Truck queue in a container terminal
clips.note: Three lanes of trucks stand nose to tail behind a stop line between container stacks. The trucks do not move during the clip; a container handler works to the right, outside the marked lanes. What holds the queue is outside the frame. This is an oblique view inside a terminal, not a top-down view of a public road, so the speed scale is rough for the distant trucks; a standing truck still reads 0 km/h.

clips.title: Four-lane highway, dense slow traffic
clips.note: Cars, a van and a tractor-trailer fill all four lanes and keep rolling in the same direction, at roughly 10 to 25 km/h if the footage plays at real speed. Nothing stands still and no obstruction is visible, but this is far below highway speed. The CV calls the road clear because every vehicle is above its 10 km/h moving threshold; whether heavy, slow traffic counts as clear is the dispatcher's call. Vehicles fill so much of this close view that the camera-motion estimate follows the traffic instead of the ground, so this clip treats the hovering camera as still.

clips.title: Floodwater across a lane
clips.note: A narrow lane runs from the left edge to the bottom of the frame, where floodwater pours across it and covers the rest of its length. Fields and buildings on both sides are under water. No vehicle is in view, so the CV, which only tracks vehicles, has nothing to measure and stays inconclusive; the dispatcher can see the water and decide. This is a village lane, not a highway, and the depth of the water cannot be read from above.

clips.title: Divided highway, light traffic
clips.note: Cars and a bus move freely on all three carriageways. No obstruction is visible on the photographed stretch; this does not establish road safety beyond the frame.

clips.title: City expressway, light traffic
clips.note: A few vehicles travel in both directions with wide gaps. No obstruction is visible on either carriageway.

clips.title: Motorway beside a truck rest area
clips.note: Dozens of trucks stand still in the rest areas on both sides, outside the marked motorway. Traffic on the motorway itself keeps moving. Counting every stationary truck in frame would wrongly suggest a jam; the road region prevents that.
